0006_0053: Ff. 1r-24v: love, praise and riddle verses that the compiler, the patron and their correspondents send each other in cipher, each followed by its solution; among them a verse petition for allowances on the compiler's return to Syria (13v), the tashifi run of two poems (14v-16v) and the first five verses of al-Jawlani's eight-verse riddle (20r-20v, continued on f. 47r across the misbound quire). The first cipher (1r) lost its plaintext to damage, and the two pieces on 12v carry none.
0054_0077: Ff. 25r-36r: verses, riddles and rhymed prose exchanged with the patron, including the red-glossed piece on f. 31r. The cipher on f. 30v (30v.7) is the only one in this range with no plaintext anywhere in the book.
0078_0101: Ff. 37r-48r: al-Jawlani's verse praising 'Taj al-Din, scion of al-Durayhim' for solving ciphers (38v-39r), his verse praising Ibn Fadl Allah (39r-39v), a cant text in the qalam qummi (37v), the compiler's verses on being excused from the vizierate of al-Sham (45v-46r, and 46v continued on the misbound f. 13r) and the last three verses of the riddle (47r).
0102_0125: Ff. 49r-60v: an exchange of short cipher verses between the compiler and the patron, with a few brought by others: the verses on 49r solved only 'after much toil', the compiler's own verse with the name Ibn Durayhim and his defence of it (49v-50r), and seven red-glossed pieces (51v-59v).
0126_0149: Ff. 61r-72v: a riddle of opposite imperatives (61r), the patron's verse sent after his brother's death (62r), a bawdy couplet enciphered twice on f. 63v, in signs and in the tree script, ciphers from and to Shihab al-Din al-Mutarjim, and one from Amin al-Din, qadi of Hama.
0150_0173: Ff. 73r-84r: petitions about a chancery decree (73v-74v), one verse enciphered twice in two pens (76v-77r), verses that allude to the names of scripts and are recorded in the Kitab al-Ajwiba al-Shamiyya (80r-81r), and a cipher whose word dividers are themselves a cipher letter (83r).
0174_0197: Ff. 85r-96r: eight red-glossed pieces; exchanges in which the compiler sends a verse of al-Mutanabbi and the patron answers in cipher on the same rhyme (93v, 95r-96r); a cipher with optional words (94v); a line on Alexandria in the 730s AH (86r). The second line of the plaintext of 88v.10 is lost in a hole in the paper.
0198_0217: Ff. 97r-106r: three red-glossed pieces, the maqlub (letter-reordering) cipher of the nazir of Qatya with the compiler's mention of 'my book Miftah al-kunuz' (102v-103r), and a riddle in deliberately odd words (105v); the plaintext of 98v.10 fits its cipher only in part. The last cipher in the volume (106v) has its own page.
